body:
Just going off of the video, I would expect every download that is done to immediately disappear from the bottom list and appear in the top list. (or give the downloaded item a hardcoded second or two at 100% for that extra completionist feel.)

How (or if at all) does this UI work with custom templates?

> I would expect every download that is done to immediately disappear from the bottom list and appear in the top list. (or give the downloaded item a hardcoded second or two at 100% for that extra completionist feel.)

Currently the tree only updates all at once, because it's simpler. Moving items would require some logic to determine _where_ to drop the element, which involves Tree searching and re-creating branches as necessary. I decided it's not worth it.

> How (or if at all) does this UI work with custom templates?

It doesn't. At most I can add a Unknown/Extra category in Installed tree that lists unrecognized files.

> > I would expect every download that is done to immediately disappear from the bottom list and appear in the top list. (or give the downloaded item a hardcoded second or two at 100% for that extra completionist feel.)
> 
> Currently the tree only updates all at once, because it's simpler. Moving items would require some logic to determine _where_ to drop the element, which involves Tree searching and re-creating branches as necessary. I decided it's not worth it.

Can't you just update / recreate the whole tree every time something finishes downloading? We're talking about milliseconds of freeing and instantiating new nodes, are we not?

> Can't you just update / recreate the whole tree every time something finishes downloading?

No, because the files that are still downloading would lose their metadata. I'd have to transfer it somehow to the re-created tree, which also requires some extra logic.

Almost finished.

> I would expect every download that is done to immediately disappear from the bottom list and appear in the top list.

I did that in the end.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cfb9b54-9b94-4019-8778-c758de6d5cc4

I had to transfer metadata anyway, to properly display download errors. The code is terribly inefficient, but for ~30 template files it does not matter.

I think this should be ready 🤔

I updated the description and video. Definitely needs some testing, I'm not 100% sure I didn't forget anything xd
Note that this depends on #117448, as canceling downloads will result in corrupted templates and there is no way to detect that a template is corrupted (or at least I didn't implement one). See comments above for testing helpers, as obviously the new templates are not officially available.

Tested this. Thoughts:

- I was confused by the disappearing 'Available Templates' panel for older versions, and I would suggest to keep the 3 panel layout at all times. So if there are no individual templates available for download, perhaps show the 'Available Templates' panel but with one faded out item that says 'No templates available for 4.5.1-stable' (or something like that) just like the 'No templates installed.' in the Installed Templates panel. It's a bit itchy that users _are_ able to delete older templates but _are not_ able to redownload those templates using this version of the engine. I do think it makes sense, but it's a bit of an awkward asymmetry. 

- I have no idea what ICU Data is, which begs the question whether the install options should have descriptions. Probably through tooltips. While some downloads are straight forward, many of them might not be. As a matter of fact I discovered there are many more templates than I thought there were because of this PR lol. For example, I have no idea what I should pick the '_console' windows templates for, what the difference is between web and web with extensions, or why the 'Web Single-Threaded' option has 'nothreads' in its name.

- The iOS template being 3 layers deep for a single option is a bit awkward. Perhaps we can trim down the option tree to its highest common denominator for all the options (should there be others like this in the future, or at least to Mobile > iOS for this particular case. For both the available and installed templates.

- The Android template was missing from the list for me. Not sure why.

- The 'Open in Web Browser' immediately started downloading the full template package for me, which was unexpected. I expected it to open a web page where I could see the individual downloads or something. Not sure where you want to go with that button?

- Likewise, what would people need the URL for that you get from 'Get Mirror URL'?

- Instead of making the Install Templates button disappear while downloading, perhaps disable the button and give it the text 'Downloading Templates...'?

- I didn't try to see how installed custom templates look in the window, but I assume it'll show up in the Installed Templates overview? How can one differentiate between official and custom templates there?

- Maybe change 'Engine Version' To 'Godot Version'?

- I can't make the engine version panel wider and it cuts off custom engine version names. Not sure if it's worth addressing because the tooltip does still show it, but just thought I'd mention it.

- The 'download missing files' and 'download missing template' functionality is great!

- When you hover over a download in progress in both the Available templates and Installed Templates windows, the progress disappears.

- When there's downloads in progress, you can still select items in the Available Templates panel... but you can't queue the downloads then. And when the downloads are complete, the selection also disappears. All in all a bit awkward.

> which begs the question whether the install options should have descriptions. Probably through tooltips.
> ICU Data
> _console' windows templates

These two are on different level. ICU Data is "template" while "_console" files are files (part of a template). I was considering adding descriptions for templates, but not for each individual file, not sure if it's worth it. The file list is also folded by default, because normally you don't need to interact with them. It's there for extra info for advanced users.

> The 'Open in Web Browser' immediately started downloading the full template package for me, which was unexpected. I expected it to open a web page where I could see the individual downloads or something. Not sure where you want to go with that button?

That's the plan, but there is no such webpage yet :P See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117072#discussion_r2937533257

> Likewise, what would people need the URL for that you get from 'Get Mirror URL'?

idk, this option was there before. Could be useful for troubleshooting purposes maybe.

> I didn't try to see how installed custom templates look in the window, but I assume it'll show up in the Installed Templates overview?

You can't install custom templates. They are usually configured in export presets (unless people actually do copy them to the templates folder?).

> I can't make the engine version panel wider and it cuts off custom engine version names. Not sure if it's worth addressing because the tooltip does still show it, but just thought I'd mention it.

Yeah, I was considering adding another SplitContainer, but thought that the list is wide enough by default 🤷‍♂️

> When you hover over a download in progress in both the Available templates and Installed Templates windows, the progress disappears.

That's because of hover style taking over. Not sure how to resolve that, it can be changed only for the whole Tree.

The Get Mirror URL option and the Open in Web Browser kind of lead to the same thing. I'd probably remove the Get Mirror URL option until there is actual demand.

> > I didn't try to see how installed custom templates look in the window, but I assume it'll show up in the Installed Templates overview?
> You can't install custom templates. They are usually configured in export presets (unless people actually do copy them to the templates folder?).

Admittedly I did this for Rift Riff when we needed a cherrypick fix for a specific platform. But generally I agree that the custom template field in the export preset should be used. And yeah, I tend to agree that those shouldn't be part of this window. But when someone makes a custom build of Godot + templates, those _will_ show up, right?

> I'd probably remove the Get Mirror URL option until there is actual demand.

That would make a menu with single option 🤔 I guess it could be a simple button then.

> But when someone makes a custom build of Godot + templates, those will show up, right?

Editor and templates are separate builds that don't know about each other. But if you have a custom build, you can easily add custom templates to the list, by modifying the `_initialize_template_data()` method. (this can also be easily extended to add templates via plugins, but that's something for a new proposal)
I guess what I was getting at was this: … which seems fine.

Everything should be addressed now. Except > Instead of making the Install Templates button disappear while downloading, perhaps disable the button and give it the text 'Downloading Templates...'? It's easier to hide the button than to manage it's text/disable logic. I don't feel like fighting with it anymore xd

- I think this was a bug (didn't catch it on film, couldn't reproduce it again later...): I initiated a download for all windows platforms, but then when one of the files from a template was done, the entire template was moved to the installed template panel. The download progress for the remaining files did also show in the installed templates panel though.
- Just so I understand, when there are no available templates it currently shows the message 'Downloads are only available for the current Godot version.' – does that mean that if users are running on 4.8 in the future, they can't download 4.7? That's what this wording implies right now.
- Download progress still disappears on hover. It's a minor thing, and you said it's not easy to fix, but it still feels like a bug.
- Clicking on the download error warning icon spawns a real cute window. The main text in there is missing a dot at the end of sentences.
- After selecting a bunch of templates and clicking on 'Install Selected Templates', if the download failed because the mirror didn't connect or whatever, the selection is gone and I have to reselect all the templates I wanted to download. perhaps the selection should be kept (to the extent possible)?
- Sorry, I'm gonna be annoying and convince you that we do need a 'Download in progress' indicator somewhere :P Could be the download button but with different text and disabled, a label that appears when the download button is hidden, or maybe even a progress label / bar that indicates the progress of all downloads combined. I think it's necessary because the 'download state' of this panel essentially disables its main functionality and can make it unclear what you can 'do'.
- You can close the panel and downloads will just continue in the background. I'm on the fence over whether this is desired behavior or not, because then users will have no indication of whether they internet is being clogged or not :P However, it's nice to be able to just initiate the downloads and continue your merry way in the editor too. But perhaps there should be some sort of indicator that downloads will continue even if you close the window.
- Definitely a bug: when you close the editor while a download is in progress, the template will be indicated as 'installed' upon opening the editor again.
- Building on top of the above two points, perhaps there should also be a popup when a user tries to quit the editor asking whether the user wants to wait for the download to complete (and if so, open the templates panel) or cancel the download.

> does that mean that if users are running on 4.8 in the future, they can't download 4.7? That's what this wording implies right now.

Yes. We'd need to keep a template list history for each version to support downloading from earlier versions.

> But perhaps there should be some sort of indicator that downloads will continue even if you close the window. [...] there should also be a popup when a user tries to quit the editor asking whether the user wants to wait for the download to complete (and if so, open the templates panel)

It'll be easier for me to just not allow closing the dialog >_>

> Definitely a bug: when you close the editor while a download is in progress, the template will be indicated as 'installed' upon opening the editor again.

See #117448

Fixed the hover problem:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5e05a38-065b-4a21-8013-909383008bd7

Also checkboxes are remembered (maybe too much xd). Also the install button does not disappear.

I did a major rewrite of the implementation, the metadata is now a HashMap instead of being stored inside TreeItems. It's more reliable and less hacky (and probably more performant, due to less Variant usage).

I still need to fix background downloads (I will just disable closing the dialog).
EDIT:
Seems like the background download was supported before 🤔 I'll try to keep it somehow.
I opened #117688 and #117707 to fix the remaining problems. They are relevant for the old dialog too, so they can be separate PRs.
I found a workaround for the canceled requests problem: download the file to the cache folder and rename it once the download is successful (which is what the old dialog did...).

- The reason in the warning tooltips is always empty for me, both when I cancel and when I try to download from a mirror I can't connect to: - The warnings of cancelled downloads persist when navigating to another version – even to versions that have the templates already installed: - The selection of the specific files persists, but the 'minus state' of the root doesn't:
Fixed.

If an item has a warning (eg couldn't download) but it's collapsed under the header, the only indicator that there even is a warning is a slight yellow colorization of the text. For clarity it would help a LOT if in those cases the parent items have a warning indicator that say an item has a warning. Those warnings would not be necessary / can be hidden when the parent item is not collapsed and the item's warning icon is visible. Other than that, it is perhaps a bit unconventional to put the whole category of an architecture in the 'Installed Templates' even if you only downloaded one of its files: I would expect the Available Templates panel to have all the files inside the architectures that you _don't_ have, and the Installed Templates panel to include all the files that you don't. Now we're conflating the ideas of the two panels a bit. This isn't a hill I'd die on, but for clarity it could be desirable to have the architectures with partial files in both the available and installed templates panels and (obviously) have the installed ones at the bottom and the missing ones at the top. That way, you can also 'get rid of' the download missing templates button because that can be covered by a checkbox + download button in the top part of the UI. But perhaps I'm missing an important detail here?

> Other than that, it is perhaps a bit unconventional to put the whole category of an architecture in the 'Installed Templates' even if you only downloaded one of its files:

Well, the intention is that you are supposed to download the whole template, and if any file is missing, the template is considered damaged. Downloading individual files is for advanced users (you may want e.g. only debug builds).

I see that point of view and tend to agree. I can imagine some users might see it differently because you do have the option to download specific files within an architecture and nothing in this UI really indicates that individual file downloading is for advanced users. But, like I said, this isn't a hill I'd die on.

I pushed another commit that makes this PR work with the official templates. They are downloaded using partial request magic, which work by requesting parts of the TPZ archive. This only changes the internals, the dialog itself still works the same.

I also removed all debug code, so this PR is _technically_ ready to merge as is (assuming the implementation is correct xd). To test the PR, change `mirrors_metadata_url` to use e.g. `4.6.stable` instead of `GODOT_VERSION_FULL_CONFIG`.

> I pushed another commit that makes this PR work with the official templates. They are downloaded using partial request magic, which work by requesting parts of the TPZ archive.

This is very clever (didn't know it was even possible), but I would prefer if official archives were split by platform. Third-party scripts (including CI that just calls `curl` or `wget`) won't bother doing what we're doing in the editor, yet they may want to save on download times and bandwidth too.

Of course, this is a moot point if we expose our downloader to the CLI, so that you can run something like `godot --install-templates windows,linuxbsd_x86_64,linux_arm64` on CI before exporting projects.

> If we want to solve this without Minizip. New Compression mode:
Compression::MODE_DEFLATE_RAW

This could be added separately, as I think it's out of scope.
Coincidentally, there is a proposal (discussion): https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/6348
It's a different action than downloading the whole template, so IMO it needs a different icon than regular download. I'm open to suggestions, it has to convey "repairing".

> Removing export templates should have a confirmation dialog, as there's no way to undo the operation. While official templates can be easily redownloaded, this is not the case if you are far away from an Internet connection, or if you installed third-party export templates.

They are moved to trash, so technically you can undo it.

> With this PR, it's no longer possible to install a .tpz file in the editor. I don't think this was used often in the 4.x days (as third-party builds that were available for multiple platforms became rarer), but it's worth noting. I originally didn't re-implement it, because the TPZ files were supposed to be gone, and now there is not much space for that. I was planning to add it in a follow-up > When in offline mode, "Error getting the list of mirrors" still shows up when using a development build after a small delay: Should be fixed. > so technically you can undo it. Added confirmation anyway. > There should be a way to remove all export templates for an associated version, so you can quickly clean up old data after upgrading to a new version. For now you can open the directory and delete it manually.
Thanks!
